Rehab-progression guidance is therefore now in hand, at least in part, and the calf work added to Tuesday's session was clinician-directed. acuteCalfInjuryJun2026.presentation: Sun 6/21 AM basketball: minor right-calf pull played through, then acute severe left-calf pain ('shot with a lacrosse ball'), difficulty bearing weight since. Classic acute medial gastrocnemius strain ('tennis leg'), at least Grade II given the can't-weight-bear onset.
acuteCalfInjuryJun2026.selfScreenJun23: Later 6/23: no swelling or bruising, calf symmetric, and the Thompson/Simmonds calf-squeeze test normal and symmetric (foot plantarflexes both sides). Complete Achilles rupture now much less likely (Boyd 2015 PMID 26622031); DVT lower probability given no swelling/asymmetry (Wells 1997 PMID 9428249). Working dx: acute medial gastrocnemius strain, likely Grade I-II.

ruleOut.test: Achilles tendon rupture - Thompson/Simmonds calf-squeeze test
ruleOut.reason: THE can't-miss diagnosis. Rupture patients can still walk and weakly plantarflex and may have no palpable gap, so it is missed unless the squeeze test is done. A radiological 'partial tear' is treated as complete until proven otherwise (Boyd 2015 PMID 26622031; Maffulli 1998 PMID 9548122, squeeze-test sensitivity 0.96).

ruleOut.test: DVT assessment - Wells score +/- Doppler ultrasound
ruleOut.reason: DVT is found in ~10% of tennis-leg presentations and can mimic or be masked by a strain. Red flags: disproportionate unilateral swelling, warmth, redness, calf >3 cm larger than the other side (Delgado 2002 PMID 12091669; Wells 1997 PMID 9428249).

If pain is out of proportion to exam with a tense/firm compartment and pain on passive stretch, seek emergency care - these are early signs; pulselessness/pallor are late (Pechar & Lyons 2016, DOI 10.1016/j.nurpra.2015.10.013).

acuteCalfInjuryJun2026.imaging: Ultrasound (first-line) or MRI to confirm location, grade, and aponeurotic/intramuscular-tendon involvement, which predicts a longer return to sport (Green 2020 PMID 33030961; Meek 2022 DOI 10.2106/JBJS.RVW.21.00183).
acuteCalfInjuryJun2026.reference: Full evidence + phased rehab in knowledge/calf-strain-rehab.md.

ptHomeProgram.reconciliationWithTheProgram: The PT's prescription is now the calf and single-leg rehab line, and the program stops writing a parallel one so the two do not stack. Three consequences. FIRST, the program's 3x/week seated calf HSR at 135 (3x8, run as 3x10 on 7/28) retires in favor of the PT's daily 3x15. Daily calf loading is a legitimate evidence-supported pattern, closer to Alfredson's 180-heel-drops-daily model than to Beyer's 3x/week HSR, and the two produced equivalent 12- and 52-week outcomes (Beyer 2015; Strong), so this is a different protocol rather than a worse one. THE DOSE IS BODYWEIGHT, confirmed by what was actually performed on 7/29. The program initially assumed a 90 lb anchor, which was invented rather than prescribed and has now been corrected everywhere. This matters because unweighted 3x15 is a much lighter calf stimulus than 3x8-10 at 135, so retiring the loaded line is a real de-load of loaded calf capacity rather than a like-for-like swap. ASK THE PT whether bodyweight is meant to stay or to progress; if it stays, the loaded single-leg raise below becomes the only loaded calf work in the week. SECOND, the loaded single-leg calf raise at BW+25 is NOT in the PT's program even though they know about it. It is kept at once weekly rather than dropped, because at roughly 1.11x bodyweight it is the only thing in either program that addresses the >=1.0x BW knee-extended strength benchmark gating return to sport (Green 2022 PMID 35032233), and a bodyweight hold does not reach that strain. Flag it for the PT and defer if they want it out. THIRD, daily step-backs off a box with a forward chest lean are controlled stair-descent loading, which supersedes the program's own more conservative note that there should be no heel drop below neutral until stair descent is pain-free. That gate was the program's, the PT's judgment is more current, and theirs governs. The single-leg RDL also replaces the Glute-Ham Raise / Ham Curl line for hamstring volume: hip-dominant, single-leg, calf-sparing, and it exposes left versus right.
openQuestions: What grade is the strain, and did anything get measured?
What load do they intend for the daily seated calf raise 3x15 and the single-leg RDL 3x8?
Do they want the BW+25 loaded single-leg calf raise to continue?

Do they agree with the hop and capacity criteria (~20 symptom-free single-leg hops, >=30 calf raises at <=10% asymmetry) as the gate for running, plyos, and a return to basketball, or do they have their own return-to-sport criteria? If they have their own, theirs govern.

glp1ForBodyComposition.question: Whether a GLP-1 receptor agonist is worth considering to reach the body-composition targets of 210 lb and 15 percent body fat.
glp1ForBodyComposition.status: Open. This is a physician decision and the program does not recommend for or against it.
glp1ForBodyComposition.currentNumbers: 6 ft 2.5 in, 222 lb, 23.5 percent body fat on 2026-08-18. BMI 28.1. Fat mass 52.2 lb, lean mass 169.8 lb.
glp1ForBodyComposition.eligibilityGate: FDA labeling for chronic weight management with semaglutide 2.4 mg and tirzepatide is BMI 30 or above, or BMI 27 or above plus at least one weight-related comorbidity such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea or cardiovascular disease. At BMI 28.1 he falls in the second bracket, so eligibility depends on a comorbidity. He is described as non-hypertensive and has no diabetes on record, and NO LIPID PANEL HAS EVER BEEN RUN. The lipid panel already requested in knowledge/supplements.md is therefore the gate on whether this is even on the table. Get it before the conversation.
glp1ForBodyComposition.leanMassEvidence: The SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy (Look et al. 2025, Diabetes Obes Metab 27:2720-2729, PMID 39996356, n=160, 72 weeks) found body weight down 21.3 percent, fat mass down 33.9 percent and lean mass down 10.9 percent on tirzepatide. Approximately 75 percent of the weight lost was fat and 25 percent was lean. The placebo group showed the same 75/25 split, so that proportion is what weight loss does rather than a drug effect. A STEP 1 exploratory DXA analysis (n=140) showed fat mass down 19.3 percent and lean mass down 9.7 percent on semaglutide 2.4 mg. Across recent GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP trials, lean soft tissue was 26 to 40 percent of the weight lost.
glp1ForBodyComposition.whatItMeansForHim: At the observed 75/25 split, losing the 22 lb of fat needed to reach 15 percent would mean roughly 29.6 lb of total loss, of which about 7.4 lb is lean. That is 4.4 percent of his current lean mass, and lean mass is the engine for goals 2 and 3, strength and power and the vertical jump. Set against that: lower body weight reduces achilles tendon load, and CLAUDE.md Section 6 already identifies relative strength as the primary limit on his vertical jump, so 22 lb of fat off a 222 lb frame is a genuine performance gain if the lean mass holds.
glp1ForBodyComposition.whatProtectsLeanMass: Resistance training and adequate protein, both of which are in the program's control rather than the drug's. A case series of three patients emphasizing resistance training and high protein recorded lean soft tissue changes of -6.9, +2.5 and +5.8 percent, so two of three gained lean tissue during GLP-1 weight loss. Protein guidance is unchanged at 1.6 to 2.2 g per kg per day, which is 160 to 220 g at his weight.
glp1ForBodyComposition.programRecommendationIfHeProceeds: Switch body-composition measurement from the consumer BIA scale to DXA. BIA misestimates absolute fat mass against DXA and cannot resolve a 7 lb lean-mass question. Keep the resistance training running throughout, because it is the main defence for lean mass. Report lean mass, not just weight.

recommendedFollowUpFromJuly2025Panel.reason: Hyperthyroidism is one of the most common drivers of elevated SHBG. Jul 2025 panel showed SHBG 83 (upper limit 50). Rule out thyroid driver before attributing high SHBG to genetic/idiopathic.
Liver synthesizes SHBG. Elevated enzymes or altered liver function can increase SHBG. Rule out liver-driven elevation.
Low-insulin states elevate SHBG. Given mixed metabolic picture, worth characterizing insulin sensitivity.

recommendedFollowUpFromJuly2025Panel.test: Repeat T panel in 3-6 months with free T + SHBG + Estradiol + Prolactin
recommendedFollowUpFromJuly2025Panel.reason: Confirm the elevated-SHBG pattern is persistent, not a one-time reading. Same collection protocol (morning, fasted, pre-exercise, not within 2-3 weeks of Power Red donation).

testosteroneHistory.notes: Reference range 40s: 264-916 ng/dL. Within normal. Collection time unknown - if drawn afternoon, AM equivalent would have been higher since T is ~50% lower PM vs AM.
Optimal morning collection. Above age-40 average (~500-600 ng/dL). Free T and SHBG not drawn - limited interpretation without them (see 2025-07 panel showing high-SHBG pattern).

testosteroneHistory.freeTestosteroneFlag: low-normal (at floor, 3.4 pg/mL above deficiency threshold)
testosteroneHistory.notes: KEY FINDING: elevated SHBG (83 vs upper limit 50) is pulling total T out of circulation. Total T 811 is upper-normal but free/bioavailable T are at the BOTTOM of range. This is a 'functionally low-T presentation' despite robust total T. Technically does not meet the clinical cutoff for low testosterone (free T above the floor, no reported symptoms). Borderline high estradiol tracks with high total T (aromatization). Prolactin normal rules out pituitary cause. Next step: understand SHBG driver - thyroid (TSH + free T4), liver (AST/ALT/bilirubin), metabolic (fasting insulin / HbA1c). Source: Quest Diagnostics ZD478125F Men's Hormone Panel Expanded, ordering physician MARKS, Lianne, PWN Health.

nutritionGoals.primary: Steady fat loss preserving lean mass, strength, and game performance
nutritionGoals.rationale: Apr 20 body-comp overview showed +4.7 lbs fat / +1.9 lbs lean over 6 weeks. Initial 2-day/week deficit-at-BMR approach (set Apr 20 AM) was recalibrated later that day based on Helms 2014 and Aragon 2017 ISSN evidence: (1) rest-day target at BMR was more aggressive than needed, (2) intermittent restriction is not superior to daily small deficits per ISSN 2017, (3) weekly deficit was below the Helms 0.5%/wk floor anyway. Revised to moderate-deficit across 3 non-heavy-training days.
nutritionGoals.retiredReason: RETIRED at the Week 23 review, athlete's decision. Both goals are withdrawn, not paused. The calorie-anchor goal had zero logged compliance for 91 days, since 5/11, across two revisions of its anchor days, and the 8/4 review had already named the problem: recalibrating a target with no measured compliance is bookkeeping, not intervention. The restaurant cap was retired alongside it rather than kept as the low-friction survivor, because it had no logged compliance either. WHAT THIS MEANS GOING FORWARD: nutrition comes out of the science-review checklist and out of the site's daily summary bar. No calorie or protein targets are asserted, no anchor days, and reviews stop reporting a nutrition gap. Body composition stays tracked separately via bodyLog weight and body-fat readings, which is now the only lens on the recomposition goal, and the athlete.targetWeight of 210 lb and targetBodyFatPct of 15 are unchanged. If intake ever gets logged again this can be rebuilt from the superseded records below, which keep the full Helms 2014 and Hall 2019 reasoning intact.

supersededGoals.name: Moderate-deficit days
supersededGoals.supersededReason: Retired at the Wk 23 review. Zero logged compliance for 91 days across two anchor-day revisions.
supersededGoals.weeklyDeficitEstimate: ~900-2,100 cal/week = ~0.3-0.6 lb/week fat loss (within Helms 2014 0.5-1%/week lean-preserving range)
supersededGoals.rationale: REVISED 8/4 for the current week shape. Tue = rest day, PT calf block only, no lifting and no game since basketball is in its off-season. Wed = upper body only, no lower-body demand, which is the exact rationale that used to justify Thursday. Sat = pre-Sunday-game rest day, PT block only. Mon and Thu carry the barbell lower work and the graded run and stay at maintenance to fuel it; Sun stays at maintenance as the game day. SUPERSEDES the Mon/Thu/Sat scheme, whose rationale had gone stale in every clause: it read Mon as a no-training recovery day when Mon now carries the heaviest session of the week, it held Tue at maintenance as a game day when there is no Tue game, and it anchored the deficit around a Wed heavy TB DL that has moved. Daily deficit of 300-500 cal below TDEE preserves lean mass per Helms 2014.
supersededGoals.evidence: Helms et al. 2014, JISSN (PMID 24864135): 0.5-1% BW/week loss rate for lean-mass preservation in resistance-trained athletes. Aragon et al. 2017 ISSN position stand (PMID 28630601): intermittent restriction not superior to daily small-deficit approach.
supersededGoals.revisedNote: Anchor days moved Mon/Thu/Sat to Tue/Wed/Sat on 2026-08-04 (Wk 22 science review) to match the post-injury week shape.

supersededGoals.name: Restaurant meal cap
supersededGoals.supersededReason: Retired at the Wk 23 review alongside the calorie goal. Cheaper to track than macros, but it was never tracked either.
supersededGoals.rationale: Hall 2019 ward study (Cell Metab) showed ultra-processed/restaurant food environments drive ~+500 cal/day spontaneous intake vs matched whole-food diets. Current pattern: 5-7 restaurant meals/week consistently drives 3,000+ cal days. Capping at 3 fixes the weekly caloric creep without daily macro tracking.

supersededGoals.name: Deficit rest days (original Apr 20 AM)
supersededGoals.supersededReason: Target was at BMR (~1,990 cal) which was more aggressive than needed. Math using rest-day TDEE (~2,400) showed actual deficit was only 300-400 cal per day = 600-800 cal/week, below the Helms 0.5%/week floor anyway. Revised to gentler 3-day approach.

trapBarDeadlift.horizonNote: Re-horizoned 2026-08-10 (Wk 23 review) from 18 to 24 months, due 2028-03-08. The numbers were kept and the calendar moved, because the shortfall is lost training time rather than a bad rate: roughly 10 of the program's first 23 weeks were absorbed by two travel gaps and a 6-week calf layoff with 40 days of no barbell lower. At 205 today against a 245 pre-injury peak, 385 needed 14 lb/month on the old horizon against a 2-5 lb/month reality-check band (Section 7); 24 months brings it to about 9 lb/month, which is still ambitious and assumes the compliance problem gets fixed.

backSquat.horizonNote: Re-horizoned 2026-08-10 (Wk 23 review) from 18 to 24 months, due 2028-03-08. Same reasoning as the trap bar. This is the least likely of the three to land: squat is the hardest lift to progress in-season (Baker 2001 PMID 11710401, ~30-40% slower on lower body during a season), it sits at 135 against a 160 pre-injury peak, and it lost the most calendar. Treat 315 as the direction and the near-term milestone as reclaiming 160.

benchPress.horizonNote: Re-horizoned 2026-08-10 (Wk 23 review) from 12 to 18 months, due 2027-09-08. The most realistic of the three, and the only lift that kept progressing through the injury layoff: 135 in April to a clean 4x5 at 165 on 8/6. Observed rate over the last two months is 4-5 lb/month, which is squarely inside Section 7's months 6-12 band. 225 needed 8.7 lb/month on the 12-month horizon; 18 months brings it to about 4.7, which the observed rate actually supports.

activityLog.activity: Power Red (Double Red Cell) blood donation
activityLog.details: Apheresis donation, AM. Two units of packed red cells removed; plasma and platelets returned with saline. Logged as a physiological event for load context, not as a training or recovery session.
activityLog.notes: Donated a double red-cell unit today, which removes roughly twice the red cells of a normal donation. Expect reduced aerobic capacity for several weeks, not just the usual few days. A bigger red-cell deficit takes longer to rebuild than the blood volume itself. Iron intake speeds the rebuild and limits the cumulative hit across repeat donations. It doesn't fast-track this donation's own recovery though. Plan on 4-6 weeks back to full aerobic capacity rather than the usual 3-4. This matters because Phase 3 opens this week. Sunday is a basketball-and-hockey double on a system that hasn't recovered yet.

Sunday AM basketball, 30 minutes at high intensity. About 24 hours after yesterday's blood donation, while the body still re-expands blood volume. Court sport leans on quick bursts more than sustained endurance. The impact was smaller than a pure aerobic test would show. Wind was noticeably down, but the legs still felt fine. That's the expected split between aerobic and muscular systems after a donation. No lightheadedness, no elevated resting heart rate, no red flags. Achilles quiet, 0/10. Slept fine. Hockey follows this evening, a second high-intensity session on the same reduced system.

That reversal is the expected cost of a second hard session on a reduced red-cell count. Oxygen delivery lags, and hockey's sustained skating taxes the aerobic system harder than basketball's stop-start pace. No lightheadedness, just fatigue, no red flags. Vertical jump baseline still hasn't been captured, the fourth-plus deferral. Sleep and achilles not reported for either session today. Note: tonight's box jumps plus tomorrow's plyo put jumping on back-to-back days on tight calves, plus tonight's heavy deadlift. Watch the achilles Friday, trim jump volume if it flares.

Sunday AM basketball. This is the injury: early in the run, a minor pull in the right calf that was played through. A few minutes later, sudden sharp pain in the left calf, described as being hit with a lacrosse ball. This is the classic presentation of an acute calf strain. Play stopped. Since then (6/21-6/23): hard to bear weight or walk, resting, taking ibuprofen. Not bearing weight means a clinician must rule out an Achilles rupture and a blood clot first. Programming waits on that. A clinical evaluation is now an open item. Full detail on the injury and the rehab plan is in the calf-strain reference file.

activityLog.details: Left medial gastrocnemius strain, day 3. Protected weight-bearing, relative rest, elevation, ibuprofen for pain. No calf loading yet, just pain-free ankle pumps and gentle dorsiflexion range of motion. No Tuesday basketball.
activityLog.notes: Day 3 of protected loading. Top priority: an in-person exam. Rule out an Achilles rupture, check for a blood clot, and grade the strain by ultrasound. Short-course ibuprofen for pain is reasonable; fine to switch to acetaminophen as pain eases. Program impact: the power block is paused. Calf loading drops to zero this week, then rebuilds gradually rather than jumping back to pre-injury loads. The achilles pain-free streak is paused, not lost. Self-check later today: no visible swelling or bruising, the calf isn't lopsided. The calf-squeeze test was normal and symmetric, both good signs against a rupture or clot. Working assessment: a mild-to-moderate calf strain. Proceeding into the rehab block; a professional grading exam is recommended but not urgent. Watch for swelling, warmth, redness, one-sided symptoms, or pain out of proportion. Sleep and protein not reported. The week 16-18 rehab schedule is written into the plan.

Upper body session, keeping the upper-body progression alive while the lower block stays paused for the calf strain (day 4). Bench 4x4 at 160, the first time above the 155 ceiling held since May, a 5 lb step up. DB push press held at 35s, up from 30. Seated cable row ran a higher-rep ramp (130/135/140) than the one prior data point for this lift. No calf or HSR work, correct for this stage of rehab. Worth flagging: today's push press uses a leg dip-and-drive that loads the calf, the motion to avoid this early on. Strict overhead press, no leg drive, is the safer choice until the calf clears basic isometric work. Sleep and calf pain not yet reported.

Calf-rehab-week upper day. Strict overhead press substituted for the push press to avoid loading the ankle through the healing calf. Bench 4x5 at 160, full prescribed reps at last week's top weight, the first clean session at this target. Seated calf raise ran 3x10 at 95, the held rehab load for the week.

activityLog.details: Daily double-leg calf raises through the week. Monday: first de-loaded calf work plus isometrics. Tuesday: calf-sparing lower body. Wednesday: calf hold plus upper. Friday: soleus plus a second calf-sparing lower session. Progressing into single-leg calf raises next week.
activityLog.notes: End-of-week recall for the calf rehab, exact daily numbers weren't captured. Some pain during sessions, but strength is returning. Stair descent is less painful than it was, previously sharp and unpredictable on certain steps. Without exact daily pain scores the 24-hour recovery rule can't be checked precisely, but the overall trend reads positive.

Sunday PM hockey, an off-plan return to sport. The plan had today as rest, with games gated until the return-to-sport tests were passed. Played through with light, tolerable left-calf pain, did not stop. Day 14 post-injury, still an early loaded-strength stage. Hockey is a later-stage activity. It skipped the tests meant to come first: a capacity test, a hop test, cutting. Hockey's push-off and cutting are the same motion that caused the injury. Finishing a full game with only light pain is a good sign and suggests a milder strain. It doesn't retroactively pass the tests still needed. Recurrence risk stays real at this age with a calf injury on record. Morning-after: light soreness on waking, already easing, passing the 24-hour rule. One clean game is encouraging, but isn't full clearance. Duration, intensity and pain score weren't captured.

exercises.name: Single-leg calf-raise to fatigue (capacity test)
exercises.notes: Clears the 30-rep, 10%-asymmetry bar on raw count, but the athlete reported less strength and less height on the left. Treat as encouraging, not a confirmed clean pass. Not a fully standardized test.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (soleus, bodyweight)
exercises.weight: bodyweight (from a chair, no external load)
exercises.notes: Reduced from last week's 95 lb to bodyweight. The planned standing single-leg and weighted soleus work were skipped.

activityLog.notes: Monday rehab: a capacity test plus most of the planned loaded work. Key result: single-leg calf-raise to fatigue, 30 reps left, 30 right. That clears the 30-rep, 10%-asymmetry bar on raw count. But the athlete felt less force and height on the left. Equal counts overstate how even the sides are, and it wasn't fully standardized. Treat it as encouraging, not confirmed; re-test on a clean morning. Loaded-strength, hop, and cutting tests are still untested. Loaded work: seated calf raises at bodyweight, down from 95 lb; standing single-leg and weighted soleus work skipped. One pain event: leaning bodyweight over a foot propped on a curb produced a sharp jolt. That stretch is off-limits now. Achilles stayed pain-free. Slept 7-8 hours. Morning-after: some calf soreness plus new hamstring tenderness, worth watching. Today's basketball: play only if the calf warms up clean.

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.notes: Worked up to 165 for 5 on the last two sets, the next step from last week's clean 160.

exercises.name: Strict Overhead Press
exercises.notes: Switched to barbell from dumbbells. 95 for 5, then 75 for 8 on the back-off sets.

exercises.name: Bent Over Barbell Row
exercises.notes: Substituted for the planned seated cable row. Ramped 75, 95, 105.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (HSR)
exercises.notes: Ramped to 135, above the rehab plan's held load of 95.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise (HSR)
exercises.notes: Standing, full floor range, slightly above the prescribed bodyweight plus 20.

activityLog.notes: Wednesday upper and calf. Upper body progressing well. Bench ran 160/160/165/165, hitting 165 for 5 on the last two sets, the next step from last week's clean 160. Overhead press moved to barbell, 95 for 5 then 75 for 8. Bent-over row substituted for the planned seated cable row, ramped 75/95/105. Lat pulldown 95/145/145. Calf loading ran ahead of plan. Seated calf was held at 95, increases gated on clean mornings, but this session jumped to 135. Single-leg work went to bodyweight plus 25. Not a red flag alone, since 135 is under the pre-injury load. But it skipped the gate the rehab plan is built on. Tomorrow's morning read decides whether to keep building or drop back. No calf or achilles pain during the session. Morning-after: calf felt better than the day before, beating baseline. Sleep not reported.

activityLog.details: PT session for the left calf. Treatment plus a home exercise program. No capacity or strength testing done and no explicit change to clearance for hops, running, plyos, or sport.
activityLog.notes: First professional visit for the calf, 37 days after the injury. Correction to an earlier log: this wasn't just an evaluation. The physical therapist prescribed a home program. Later that day's isometric calf holds came from it, 6x30 seconds both legs plus 3x30 seconds per leg. This counts as clinician-directed rehab, which is what the open clinical-evaluation item was asking for. Still open: an official grade for the strain, and objective test numbers. Also the therapist's view on the hop and capacity tests that currently gate running, jumping, and basketball. The full home program hasn't been captured yet. Sleep reported as a range rather than a number, logged as 8 hours.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.notes: Clean at the restart load. First barbell lower session since 6/18, 40 days off, about 15% under the last working weight.

exercises.name: Back Squat

exercises.name: Isometric Standing Calf Hold (bilateral)
exercises.notes: PT-prescribed, part of the home program. Standing means the knee stays extended, biasing the gastroc.

exercises.name: Isometric Standing Calf Hold (single-leg)
exercises.notes: PT-prescribed. About 4.5 minutes of total hold time across both blocks. Doing it single-leg shows left-right differences in how steady the hold is. A hold produces no rep count or force number though.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (HSR)
exercises.notes: Ramped to 90 then held 135 for two sets. 10 reps instead of the planned 8, same shape as the prior session.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise (HSR)
exercises.notes: Skipped, though the PT-prescribed isometric holds covered some of the same ground. Still missing is the loaded version, which the isometric holds can't replace. Returns Friday.

exercises.name: Single-leg calf-raise capacity test
exercises.notes: Skipped, moved to Thursday as the session finisher.

activityLog.notes: Prescribed for Monday, ran Tuesday evening after the morning's PT visit. Both barbell lower lifts came back in one session. Trap bar deadlift 4x5 at 205, clean, and back squat held 135 for two sets. A bigger first session back than planned, and 40 days off makes it the highest-uncertainty session of the block. Both coming back clean isn't a surprise; strength holds up better than muscle size after time off. Deadlift has one clean session banked, a second earns the next increase. Squat doesn't count, only 2 of 4 sets were at the restart weight. Calf work changed under clinical direction. Isometric holds added, seated calf raise ran 3x10 at 90/135/135, loaded single-leg and hamstring work skipped. Total calf load was actually higher than planned, and it stayed quiet all session. Morning-after: mild soreness, settling within 24 hours, a good tolerance signal. Capacity test skipped again, moves to Thursday. No intake data logged since May.

activityLog.activity: Upper and PT calf block (Wed Phase 3)

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.notes: Ramped 45/95/135, then 165 for 3, 5, 3, 3, the first bench work in 21 days. Only one of the four sets at 165 reached 5 reps. A clean 4x5 at 165 is still the goal. Total volume at 165 is up from last time. Hold at 165.

activityLog.notes: Upper day plus the PT's daily calf block. Bench ramped up then ran 4 sets at 165, 3/5/3/3 reps, the first bench work in 21 days. Only one set reached 5 reps, so a full clean set at 165 is still the goal. Close-grip bench substituted for the planned dumbbell press. Overhead press went seated with an empty bar instead of 95 standing, protecting the calf. But well below what seated should allow. Row ran 5x5 at 95 instead of 3x8 at 105. Pulldown and woodchop skipped. PT isometric blocks done as prescribed; seated calf ran unweighted, confirming the PT's dose is bodyweight, not 90 lb. Soreness in both lower legs, diffuse and bilateral, 3-5/10, up from 1-2/10. Likely from Tuesday's session after 40 days of near-zero calf load. Should ease by the weekend. Thursday's gate tests are postponed again, too close to a game for a clean read. No intake data logged since May.

exercises.notes: All four working sets clean, the first full clean set at this weight since the restart. One session banked, a second clean set earns the next increase. Full depth, controlled down phase.

exercises.name: Single-Leg RDL (dumbbell)
exercises.notes: PT-prescribed, 2-3 times weekly. Covers the hamstring work the skipped exercise left out, and shows left-right differences. Hinge to a hamstring stretch, flat back.

exercises.notes: PT daily block.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise

activityLog.notes: Ran as prescribed. The most informative session of this block. Three new things landed on the calf at once, and it handled them all. The soreness spike from two days ago eased as expected, both Friday and today's morning reads came in clean. What's new: step-backs finally started after being on hold since Monday. The loaded single-leg calf raise ran at bodyweight plus 25 per leg. First calf work this block to clear the loaded-strength threshold bodyweight holds can't reach. That's a lot of new load two days before a game, but the next two mornings came in clean. Squat: first clean 4x5 at 135, a second session earns the next increase. Deadlift wasn't in this session; Monday's clean session stands alone. Thursday was skipped entirely, so pulldown and woodchop never happened. The week closes with back under target and zero core work, the second week running. Sleep not reported.

Sunday PM hockey, the week's only game and the first since the earlier off-plan return. This one was on-plan, the regular scheduled game. 14 days after lower-body work restarted, 2 days after the first loaded calf work and step-backs. Hockey's push-off and cutting are the same motion that caused the injury. Tolerating a full game on top of Friday's new load is a meaningful test. Both the morning-before and morning-after reads came in clean, which is what the gate tests were waiting on. A game doesn't substitute for the actual tests. But it means Monday's tests run on a calf that has clearly handled sport load. One caveat: the tests run about 14 hours after a game. The rep count may under-read, though the asymmetry number should still be reliable. Duration, intensity, and Sunday night's sleep weren't reported.

exercises.name: Single-leg hop test (gate)
exercises.notes: Passed, 20 hops each leg, symptom-free both sides. Hop height wasn't measured, so this passes on symptoms and count, not a measured height number.

exercises.name: Single-leg calf-raise to fatigue (capacity test)
exercises.notes: Passed, 30 and 30, 0% asymmetry against a 10% ceiling. Both legs stopped at the 30-rep target rather than true failure, so this is a floor, not a ceiling.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.notes: Clean. Second consecutive clean 4x5 at 205, opens 215 next lower day.

exercises.name: Single-Leg RDL (dumbbell)
exercises.notes: PT item, second dose this week at the same load, 20 lb dumbbells.

activityLog.notes: Both gate tests passed on the first real attempt, after four earlier postponements. Day 43 post-injury, inside the expected recovery window. Hops: 20 per leg, symptom-free both sides, clearing running and box jumps. Capacity: 30 reps left and 30 right, 0% asymmetry, clearing the 30-rep and 10%-asymmetry bar. Both legs stopped right at 30, the target number, rather than true failure. This is a floor on capacity, not a ceiling. This opens graded running and step-down box jumps this week. Two of four return-to-sport criteria are now met. Still outstanding: loaded-strength benchmarks, hop-height asymmetry, and a clean cutting test, a question for the PT. Sunday basketball holds one more week. Lifting: trap bar deadlift 4x5 at 205, clean again, earning 215 next time. Single-leg RDL held at 20 lb dumbbells. Age and a prior calf injury are the two strongest recurrence risks. Calf capacity is now a permanent maintenance item. Sleep not reported.

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.notes: Clean 4x5 at 165, the first time the full prescription has landed after two earlier attempts. Opens 170 next upper day.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.notes: Prescribed 3x8 at 145. Ran instead as a ramp to one working set at 145, fewer total reps than prescribed. A step back from the prior session's performance at this weight.

exercises.name: Strict Overhead Press (dumbbell)
exercises.notes: Substituted dumbbells for the prescribed barbell press. Same load as three weeks ago, so shoulders held rather than progressing, now under target for a third week.

exercises.name: Bent Over Barbell Row
exercises.notes: Inverted grip. Prescribed 5x5 at 105 as a conservative rebuild; went to 135 instead. Not new territory, matches an old baseline. Rep drop-off across the sets suggests the last set was near failure.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.notes: Prescribed 4x5 at 95. Lost when the session shifted off Wednesday, leaving chest under target for the week.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop (Low-to-High)
exercises.notes: Prescribed 3x10/side at 30. Lost in the shift. Core stays at zero sets for a third straight week.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.notes: Prescribed 3x10/side at 30. Lost in the shift, same as the woodchop.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (HSR)
exercises.notes: Prescribed 3x10 at 135, meant to take loaded calf work to twice a week. Lost in the shift, so the week runs one loaded calf session again unless it gets rescheduled.

activityLog.notes: Wednesday's session got skipped and ran Thursday morning instead. Today carries two sessions, with the run and lower work still to come tonight. Headline result: bench 4x5 at 165, clean, the specific thing this week was waiting on, so 170 is next. Against the rest of the plan the session ran at about 60%. Four of eight planned exercises done, three of those four changed from the prescription. Volume landed below target on chest, shoulders, and core; back cleared its target for the first time in weeks. The row went 30 lb over the prescribed weight, fine since it recovers an old baseline. The rep drop-off shows it was pushed close to the edge though. The pulldown came in under the prescribed load and reps, the same lift that slipped before. Achilles and calf stayed quiet through bench and rows. Sleep not reported.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.notes: Held 205 rather than stepping to 215, the right call on a day that already carried a morning upper session. Third consecutive clean 4x5 at 205. The 215 step is still earned and moves to Monday.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.notes: Substituted for the prescribed back squat, the PT's regular squat item. Defensible as a lower-risk quad stimulus mid-rehab, since it skips the loaded ankle demand a squat puts through. But 170 is well under the pre-injury top set of 270. It's a re-entry number, and it doesn't satisfy the PT's squat prescription.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (HSR)
exercises.notes: Pulled forward from the weekend slot after Wednesday was skipped. Genuinely loaded soleus work, taking the week from one loaded calf session to two. Same load as last time, 3x10 at 90/135/135.

exercises.name: Standing Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.notes: Bodyweight, confirmed on ask, logged under its own name rather than as the loaded version. That lift's history sits at bodyweight plus 25 lb per leg against a pre-injury bodyweight plus 72. Letting today's session carry the loaded name forward would misrepresent the real progression.

exercises.name: Graded Return-to-Run (walk-jog intervals)
exercises.notes: Not done, confirmed on ask. First running since the strain, 46 days out, unlocked by Monday's hop test. It slipped past its scheduled week. The fifth slip in the same pattern the gate tests themselves took four tries to break. Moves to Monday, not stacked onto Friday since Friday already carries the first jumps in 47 days.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.notes: Prescribed as the PT's regular squat item. Replaced by leg press, see above.

activityLog.notes: Second session of the day, following the upper work that shifted off Wednesday. Barbell lower held at 205 rather than stepping to 215, keeping today's morning read attributable to one thing. The loaded soleus dose finally landed: seated calf raise 3x10 at 135. First genuinely loaded seated calf work since the strain. Takes the week from one loaded session to two. The run did not happen, confirmed on ask. It moves to Monday instead of stacking onto Friday, since Friday already carries the first box jumps in 47 days. Standing single-leg raises were bodyweight, also confirmed. The honest count for loaded calf work this week is one session, not two. The gastroc's loaded dose is still outstanding. Volume: quads 3 sets, posterior chain 4 sets, calf 6 sets across two movements but only 3 loaded. Not reported: sleep for Wednesday night, and whether the PT isometric holds and step-backs ran.

Non-programmed activity, same as an earlier yardwork substitution. Two hours building couch frames: standing, squatting, kneeling, lifting and carrying. Real but unstructured lower-body and grip load, not rest. This replaced the day carrying the deferred core work and the loaded single-leg calf raise. Moved off Friday so box jumps could own that day. None of it ran, and neither did the PT block. Unstructured lower-body work covers squat and hinge patterns but doesn't replicate the tendon-specific calf loading the rehab needs. Week 22 closes with one loaded calf session against the 3x/week target. Direct core stays at zero for a third week running. This also puts unstructured load about 24 hours before Sunday's hockey game. Same window a loaded session occupied before the prior game, and that was tolerated fine.

The most informative datum of the whole calf block. A full game at high intensity with regular shifts. Nothing at all in the calf or achilles during play or right after. Monday's morning read: calf 1/10, achilles 1/10. Hockey's push-off and cutting are the strain's own mechanism. A symptom-free full game is a direct test of the injured tissue, and it passed. A stronger signal than the prior game, which lacked the same detail. It doesn't substitute for the remaining return-to-sport tests. Skating has no jump landing, so it misses what box jumps and basketball impose, and loaded-strength benchmarks are still untested. Strong evidence the tissue handles sport load, not evidence every test is passed. Worth noting: the week before had only one lift day of three, no run, no box jumps. The game landed on a well-rested athlete. Day 49 post-strain. Pre-game read and sleep not reported.

Complete session, with every prescribed item at the prescribed load. Box jumps ran first, 4x3 off the 18 in box, with a step down on every rep. The left medial gastroc registered 1-3/10 during the jumps, and the next morning read 0/10. Trap bar deadlift took the 215 step, deferred since 7/28. Back squat held 135, its first outing since 7/31. Seated calf raise stepped from 135 to 150. Single-leg RDL ran 3x8 per leg at the 20s. The daily isometric and step-back block was not reported. Day 53 post-strain.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise (HSR)

activityLog.notes: First session under the two-day effort model. Bench ran 5, 5 and 8 at 170, with set 3 as the prescribed 5+ calibration set. Close grip ran 5, 5 and 10 at 95. Bent over row ran 5, 5 and 10 at 135. The third set produced sharp lower back pain, still present 30 minutes later. Lat pulldown found failure at exactly 8 reps on both sets at 145. Dumbbell overhead press ran 3x6 at the 35s. Woodchop and Pallof press both ran sets of 5 at 30 lb against a prescribed 10. The load was too heavy for the rep target. Single-leg calf raise ran 3x6 per leg at bodyweight plus 25, confirmed as a true 6RM. The achilles and both calves were symptom-free. The daily isometric block was skipped. Three reps-plus sets ran, against the one prescribed.

First basketball since the 6/21 strain, 56 days. Played 20 minutes at roughly half intensity by choice, rather than returning at full intensity. Calf and Achilles quiet throughout. The lower back held with nothing through landing and rotation. It had produced sharp pain on Friday's row and cleared over the weekend.

Second game of the day, after the morning basketball return. 60 minutes at high intensity, symptom-free start to finish. First Sunday double-header since 6/14. The lower back held through the flexed skating posture with nothing.

The third set went to 10 against a 5-rep cap. The lower back was fine this time, unlike 8/14 when the same rep count produced sharp pain. Lat pulldown found failure at 8 reps on both sets at 145, matching 8/14. Single-leg calf raise stepped to bodyweight plus 35 and ran 3x8 per leg rather than the prescribed 3x6. Eight reps were available at that load.

scienceReviews.findings:
Wk 11 / Wk 3 of Phase 2 review (13 days since last review on 2026-05-04, overdue by 6 days vs weekly cadence target).

STRENGTH PROGRESSION (Section 7 checkpoint, Wk 11 was the planned re-evaluation point).

- TB DL: 225 → 240 lb over 8 wks = 1.88 lb/wk = 8.1 lb/month. Inside Section 7 expected range (5-15 lb/month for months 0-6, intermediate). 145 lb remaining to target. At current pace, 385x5 lands ~18 months out; 12-month timeline plausible only if Phase 2 RPE 7-8 work accelerates from Phase 1 RPE 6-7.

- Back Squat: rebuilt from 45 lb pattern-work (Apr 8) to 155x4x5 (May 6). Real progression now ~5 lb/cycle. 160 lb to target. CLAUDE.md called 15-18 months more realistic than 12 for squat, current data supports that.

- Bench Press: 135 → 150 in 30 days = 3.5 lb/wk = 15.2 lb/month. Top of Section 7 range. 75 lb to target. Most realistic of the three; ~5-6 months at current pace.

HSR COMPLIANCE (the biggest miss this review).

- Wk 9: 2/3 sessions (Wed seated + Fri standing single-leg). Bonus Tue dropped vs Wk 8.

- Wk 10: 1/3 sessions (Fri only, Wed/Thu missed to work travel).

- Wk 11 to date: 0/3.

- 3 consecutive weeks below Beyer 2015 (PMID 26018970, Strong) protocol target. Wk 8 success was the bonus Tue HSR session; that pattern wasn't carried into Phase 2. Outcomes are protective so far (see Achilles), but compliance is the lagging indicator. Magnusson and Kjaer 2019 (PMC6395417, Strong) on multi-month tendon adaptation cycles argues against extended compliance gaps.

ACHILLES (the strongest signal in the program).

- 15-event green-zone (≤3/10) streak back to 2026-03-17. Zero events in yellow (4-5) or red (>5) range across past 30 days.

- Plyo introduction (5/9, 30 contacts) and ramp (5/15, 40 contacts) both completed at 0/10.

- Two plyo→game 48h clusters (Sat 5/9 → Sun 5/10; Fri 5/15 → Sun 5/17) both clean.

- Meets Section 4 criteria to continue Fri plyo block by wide margin.

PLYO BLOCK (Section 6).

- On schedule per 5/04 review forecast. Wk 9: 30 contacts (ramp floor). Wk 10: 40 contacts (+10 ramp, hitting Section 6 floor). Wk 11 prescribed 50, Wk 12 prescribed 60 (top of 40-60 range). After Wk 12 close, 2-week maintenance Wks 13-14 per Phase 3 plan.

- Markovic 2007 (Strong): ~4-8% VJ improvement from 6-12 weeks of plyo in trained athletes. The 4-week block targets the steeper portion of that curve.

VOLUME (Wk 10 anomaly).

- Wk 10 = 1 training session (Fri plyo) vs typical 3, due to work travel. Net: zero direct upper-body sets, zero non-plyo lower-body sets.

- Functionally an unscheduled reactive 'deload.' Per Coleman 2024 (PMID 38274324, Moderate), unscheduled deloads without fatigue signals can cost strength gain. But Wk 10 was sport/work-driven not fatigue-driven, and adjacent outcomes (achilles, game performance) were intact. Treat as one-off, not a pattern.

Recovery data gap.

- Sleep logged 4/14 nights (29%) since last review.

- Protein logged 3/14 days (21%).

- Body comp: 1 reading (5/7: 220.5 lb / 23.0% BF, essentially flat from 5/04 baseline of 221.3 / 23.2%).

- Per CLAUDE.md: 'Data gaps on these two fields compromise the 12-week HSR adaptation check. The Knowles 2018 sleep-intensity auto-regulation.' Now a compounded gap across two consecutive reviews (Wk 6 review also flagged this).

PHASE 2 STATUS.

- Wk 11 = Wk 3 of Phase 2. RPE targets shifted from 6-7 (Phase 1) to 7-8 (Phase 2), too early to tell if working-set RPE actually moved. The Wk 11 + Wk 13 sessions will be the read.

scienceReviews.changes:

Travel-proof (no equipment dependency beyond a step + DBs), low-CNS-cost before Tue basketball, and protects Beyer 3x/wk compliance even when Wed/Thu fall out. Pattern modeled on the Wk 8 bonus-Tue success. References: Beyer 2015 (PMID 26018970, Strong); Magnusson and Kjaer 2019 (PMC6395417, Strong) on tendon load continuity.

2) Recovery capture trigger: Standardize a single morning log: sleep hours / AM achilles 0-10 / protein floor estimate (Y/N hit 40g by lunch). Target 80% capture (≥5/7 days/week). The Silbernagel 24-hour rule and Knowles 2018 sleep-intensity auto-regulation both depend on consistent daily reads. References: Silbernagel 2007 (PMID 17307888, Strong); Knowles 2018 (PMID 29422383, Moderate); Walsh 2021 IOC consensus (PMID 33144349, Strong).

3) HOLD 12-Month strength targets through WK 14: Re-evaluate after Phase 2 plyo block closes (5/29) and 2-week maintenance Wks 13-14 complete. Current progression rates (TB DL 8.1 lb/mo, Bench 15.2 lb/mo) are inside Section 7 expected ranges. Back Squat will be the constraint and likely confirms the 15-18 month timeline CLAUDE.md flagged. Hold for now. References: Rhea 2003 dose-response meta-analysis (Moderate); Baker 2001 (PMID 11710401, Moderate) on in-season constraint.

scienceReviews.findings:
Wk 12 end-of-week / plyo-block-close review (13 days since the 2026-05-17 review. The 5/17 entry named today's checkpoint - re-evaluate Section 7 targets after the block closes 5/29). Window covered: 5/18 (Wk 11 back-half) through 5/29 (Wk 12 close).

STRENGTH (Section 7 re-evaluation - the purpose of this checkpoint).

- TB DL: held 240 for a 2nd clean session 5/20 (a 14-day layoff did NOT produce the forecast RPE bump - pattern intact). Then +5 to 245 on 5/27 (clean, first compound +5 in 4 weeks). Now 140 lb from the 385x5 target. Rate is still ~8 lb/month (Wk 11 review figure). The Phase 2 RPE 7-8 shift has not yet accelerated TB DL beyond its Phase 1 rate. At this pace 385x5 lands ~17-18 months out, NOT 12.

Honest read: TB DL 385 is an 18-month target.

- Bench: held 150 for a 2nd clean session 5/21, then +5 to 155 on 5/28 (clean, RPE 7-8). Now 70 lb from 225x5 at ~15 lb/month (Wk 11 figure) = ~4-5 months. On pace for the 12-month target and arguably ahead. Most reliable of the three.

- Back Squat: held 155 (5/20, 2nd clean session, opened 160) but the 160 push was DEFERRED on 5/27 - no squat rack available. Substituted Leg Press 3x10 (90/180/270). So an earned +5 is un-cashed and the constraint lift lost a progression to equipment, not to the athlete. 160 lb from 315x5; CLAUDE.md's 15-18 month call is confirmed by the data. Equipment availability is now a live risk for the squat specifically.

Section 7 conclusion: Bench 225 holds at 12 months (tracking ahead); TB DL 385 and Squat 315 are honestly 18-month targets at observed rates. Recommend re-horizoning rather than carrying targets the data won't support (Rhea 2003 dose-response, Moderate; Baker 2001 PMID 11710401 in-season constraint; Lexell 1995 age recovery factor).

HSR COMPLIANCE (Beyer 2015 PMID 26018970, Strong - the headline reversal).

- Wk 11: 3/3 (Wed seated + Wed single-leg + Fri single-leg). First 3/3 since Wk 8.

- Wk 12: 3/3 (Wed single-leg + Fri seated + Fri single-leg double-variant make-up).

- TWO consecutive Beyer-compliant weeks, reversing the Wk 9-11 decline (2/3 -> 1/3 -> 0/3-at-last-review). The 5/17 structural fix (restore Seated Calf to Wed) is the direct driver.

- CAVEAT: both weeks were recovered by reactive make-up, not the prescribed Mon-AM HSR mini-session. The Monday anchor (the 5/17 review's #1 fix) was NOT adopted either week (5/18 = beach walk instead, 5/25 = rest). Friday double-up works but is fragile - one forgotten Friday = a missed week. Durability still depends on the unrealized Monday anchor. Process note: the 5/17 Seated-Calf fix was added to modifiedWeeks and the activityLog but never to the base index.html prescription. Which is why Seated was missed Wed 5/27 (patched 5/27).

Fixes must land in the base prescription, not just the modified week.

VOLUME (Section 3, 6-10 hard sets/muscle/wk + sport): Both weeks in range. Wk 11 lower ~14 sets + plyo + 2 games, upper ~15 sets, calves 9 (on Beyer target), core at floor. Wk 12 lower ~13 sets (Leg Press preserved quad volume when the rack was unavailable), upper ~15 sets, calves 9. No volume concern.

ACHILLES (Silbernagel 2007 PMID 17307888, Strong): Green zone (<=3/10) unbroken back to 3/17 - now ~10+ weeks. Only nonzero in-window was 5/27 AM 1/10 (resolved with warmup, still green, no action per Section 4). The tendon tolerated the FULL plyo ramp 30 -> 60 contacts without leaving green. Strongest signal in the program that the Beyer HSR protocol is working. GAP: the 5/29 post-plyo achilles read (the single most informative point of the block - highest-load session of the week) is not yet reported.

RECOVERY / NUTRITION (Section 5).

- Sleep: IMPROVED this window - captured on 5/17, 5/20, 5/21, 5/22, 5/24, 5/26, 5/27, 5/28 (~70%, up from 29% at the Wk 11 review). No sub-6h nights; 5/27 was 7h (low-normal, NSF range, not a Section 2 trigger). The recovery-capture trigger is partially landing for sleep.

- Protein: 0% captured. bodyLog has ZERO protein entries 5/18-5/30 (only a 5/28 weight/BF reading). Worse than the 21% at the Wk 11 review. This is the binding constraint: every nutrition and recomp conclusion below is un-diagnosable without intake data (Morton 2018 PMID 28698222 distribution. The daily protein-floor read is the missing field).

- Body comp: 5/28 = 220.5 lb / 23.0% BF, IDENTICAL to 5/7. Flat at program-best for 3 weeks - holding, not regressing, but the slow-recomp has plateaued. Cannot diagnose the plateau (intake unlogged).

Plyo block close (Section 6 / Markovic 2007, Strong. Ebben 2010): Full 4-week block complete - 30 (5/9) -> 40 (5/15) -> 50 (5/22) -> 60 (5/29). Landing at the top of the 40-60 range, every session clean achilles. Markovic 2007 projects ~4-8% VJ gain over 6-12 wk; this 4-wk block targets the steep early portion. MEASUREMENT GAP: VJ is goal #3 and the plyo block is its primary driver. But there is NO pre/post vertical-jump test in the data - the block closed with no way to quantify whether it moved VJ.

Wks 13-14 = 2-week plyo maintenance per the Phase 3 plan; Phase 3 (power realization) starts Wk 15 (~Jun 14).

DELOAD: Wk 12 is a scheduled every-4th-week deload (4/8/12). Correctly SKIPPED (ran normally with 2 progressions landed) - skip-criteria all green (lifts progressing, RPE on target, achilles stable, no sub-6h sleep). Consistent with Coleman 2024 PMID 38274324 (prophylactic deloads in non-fatigued lifters cost gains). Continues the Wk 8 skip pattern. Next scheduled deload Wk 16, by which point Phase 3 is underway.

PHASE 2 -> 3 READINESS: Strong. Two +5 progressions (TB DL, Bench) landed at RPE 7-8 in Wk 12, so the Phase 2 intensity bump is tolerated and productive. Maintenance Wks 13-14 then Phase 3 is the right sequence (Section 6 diminishing returns after a 4-wk block).
scienceReviews.changes:
1) PROTEIN/INTAKE LOGGING IS THE #1 FIX (it gates every nutrition + recomp conclusion). 0% protein capture this window and body comp flat 3 weeks at program-best - the plateau is un-diagnosable without intake. Not more analysis; capture. Prioritize the single daily protein-floor read (hit 40g by lunch Y/N) above all other fields since that is the 0% gap. Target >=5/7 days. References: Morton 2018 (PMID 28698222, Strong); Schoenfeld and Aragon 2018.

2) SECTION 7 TARGET RE-HORIZON (recommendation, pending athlete sign-off - not yet written to data.targets): hold Bench 225 at 12 months (tracking ahead, ~4-5 mo). Re-horizon TB DL 385 and Squat 315 to ~18 months, which the observed rates (TB DL ~8 lb/mo, Squat the in-season constraint) actually support. Also: cash the un-cashed Back Squat 160 in Wk 13 IF a rack is available. The constraint lift should not keep losing earned progressions to equipment. References: Rhea 2003 (Moderate); Baker 2001 (PMID 11710401, Moderate); Lexell 1995.

3) Install the monday HSR anchor during wks 13-14 (durability fix): two 3/3 weeks is real, but both were fragile Friday catch-ups. Not the prescribed Mon-AM mini-session. Wks 13-14 are plyo maintenance (lower lift volume). The low-cost window to actually build the Monday HSR mini-session into habit, so compliance survives a dropped Wed/Fri. 3 sets seated plus 3 sets standing single-leg, full Beyer load/tempo. Also confirm the Seated Calf fix is now in the base index.html prescription, not just modified weeks.

References: Beyer 2015 (PMID 26018970, Strong); Magnusson and Kjaer 2019 (PMC6395417, Strong) tendon load continuity.

WORTH DOING (not a core adjustment): establish a vertical-jump baseline before Wks 13-14, so the next plyo block can be evaluated against goal #3. Use jump-reach minus standing-reach, or a phone jump-test. The block that just closed has no VJ measurement (Markovic 2007, Strong).

Open data item: the 5/29 post-plyo achilles read and Thu/Fri-night sleep are still unreported - needed to close the block record (Silbernagel 24-hour rule).

Because rupture patients can still walk and weakly plantarflex and may have no palpable gap. So it is missed unless the Thompson/Simmonds calf-squeeze test is done (Boyd 2015 PMID 26622031, Strong. Maffulli 1998 PMID 9548122 squeeze-test sensitivity 0.96). (2) DVT - present in ~10% of tennis-leg presentations (Delgado 2002.

scienceReviews.findings:
WK 21 REVIEW (Mon 7/27, Wk 21 day 2). Window 7/6 to 7/27 - a 21-day window containing a 19-day logging blackout (last entry 7/8). Everything below the athlete-reported line is inference from a gap, and is labeled as such. What actually happened (athlete-reported 7/27, not logged): travel across Weeks 19-20 with little or no training. NO barbell lower since 6/18. No games since the 7/5 hockey.

Calf loading continued but below pre-injury loads and unlogged. Bench held at 165. THE HEADLINE - The program changed shape, not just paused. Basketball is in its off-season, so the Tuesday game is structurally gone, and Sunday AM basketball is self-gated pending calf clearance. Weekly game load drops from three to one (hockey Sun PM). Section 3's in-season ceiling - 6-10 hard sets per muscle, with games contributing substantial unquantified lower-body load - was written for a three-game week.

At one game, the lower end of that range is now unnecessarily conservative and this becomes the best lower-body rebuild window the program has had. The lower-body layoff IS The biggest number: 39 days with no TB DL or back squat. Training cessation lowers all components of strength with a dose-response on duration (Bosquet 2013 PMID 23347054: maximal force SMD -0.46, submaximal strength -0.62. Maximal power -0.20 across 103 studies. Losses smaller in recreational athletes than inactive people. Moderate).

The abstract does not report percentage loss stratified by cessation duration, so restart loads are a judgment call from the effect direction. Not a figure the literature supplies - stated plainly rather than dressed up as precision. The calf, honestly: day 36, chronologically inside the knowledge base's Phase 3 window (week 5-9). The Phase 2 loaded-strength benchmarks are closer than the log suggests - 7/8's single-leg BW+25 is roughly 1.11x bodyweight. Which nominally clears the 1.0x BW knee-extended criterion. What is missing is not load, it is MEASUREMENT: the 10%-asymmetry half of every benchmark has never been measured, the hop criteria are entirely untested.

And the soleus benchmark (1.5x BW knee-flexed, roughly 330 lb at 220 lb bodyweight) is not comparable to a 135 lb seated machine load. Which does not include bodyweight. So how close he actually is remains unknown. The gating problem: he is holding off Sunday AM basketball 'until the calf is 100% healed.' Right instinct. Wrong instrument - '100%' is undefined, so the hold has no exit condition and could run indefinitely. Green 2022 (PMID 35032233) supplies the actual checklist: VAS 0/10.

Calf-raise 30 or more reps at 10% or less asymmetry. Loaded-strength benchmarks at 10% or less asymmetry. Hop/jump asymmetry 10% or less. Completed symptom-free sport-specific COD/plyo exposure. Converting the feel-based gate into that checklist is the highest-leverage action this cycle. Because it is the only thing that turns an indefinite hold into a path back.

HSR COMPLIANCE: protocol is 3x/week every week; nothing logged for 19 days. Athlete reports continued calf work below pre-injury loads. So this reads as a logging gap rather than a training gap - but it cannot be verified. And progressive calf loading is the active protection against recurrence (Green 2022), not an optional extra. UPPER (still the healthy line): bench held at 165, and because 7/8 was 160/160/165/165. A clean 4x5x165 has not actually happened yet - that is the next step, then 170.

Chest volume is 4 sets from barbell bench alone, below the 6-10 range; DB bench has not been logged since 4/7. Back sits at 6 sets (row 3 plus pulldown 3), right at the floor. Core last logged 6/10. BODY COMP: no reading since 6/12 (219.5 lb, 22.7% BF) - 45 days, the longest gap of the program. Three weeks of near-inactivity plus travel is precisely the window where recomp reverses, and there is no data either way. NUTRITION: the 7/6 review released the rest-day calorie hold because hockey had resumed.

Sport then stopped for three weeks, so that release should have REVERSED and did not - through a travel-and-layoff stretch. Calories belong at the rest-day end. With lifting resuming this week, re-anchor to training days. Protein still 0% logged since 5/11, now roughly 11 weeks. ACHILLES: the tendon remains the non-problem - 0/10 on both logged readings (7/6, 7/8). Green-zone streak still paused pending the strain clearing, not lost.

DELOAD: Week 20 was the scheduled 4th-week deload and was involuntarily deloaded by travel anyway. Week 21 needs the opposite. Section 2 already holds that prophylactic calendar deloads in non-fatigued lifters reduce strength gains (Coleman 2024 PMID 38274324). After a detraining stretch, deloading would compound the loss. Next scheduled deload Week 24 (Aug 16-22) - contingency, not command. The phase label was fiction: the site read 'Phase 3: Power Realization' throughout the layoff.

Power realization requires plyometrics and explosive work, all of which are gated behind untested hop criteria. SITE STALENESS (the mechanical finding): with no modifiedWeeks entry past 19. The renderer falls back to the pre-injury default week - Wed 'Lower Body - Heavy', Fri 'Lower Moderate + Plyo'. Sun basketball AM and hockey PM. So for roughly two weeks the live site prescribed plyometrics. Unmodified heavy lower to an athlete five weeks off a gastroc strain with barbell lower frozen.

The absence of a week entry is not neutral; it is an active fallback to the pre-injury plan. DATA GAPS, ranked: (1) hop criteria and asymmetry never measured - the gate itself. (2) morning-after pain reads not logged since 7/9, despite being the designated governor since 7/6. (3) per-session calf loads unlogged for 19 days. (4) body comp 45 days. (5) protein 11 weeks.

(6) sleep logged once in six weeks (7/6).
scienceReviews.changes:
1) Barbell lower restarts this week at reduced load: TB DL 205 (from 245), Back Squat 135 (from 160). Split across Mon and Fri so each lower day carries one barbell compound rather than stacking both after 39 days off. Weights are set EXPLICITLY rather than left to carry-forward, specifically so the pre-injury 245/160 cannot leak through as this week's target. Two clean sessions earn +10. 2) Separate barbell lower from plyos IN THE GATING - this is the substantive reframe. Barbell lower is not the calf risk: TB DL is hip-dominant, and the squat bottom has the knee flexed, which slackens the biarticular gastroc.

The opposite of the injury mechanism of sudden knee extension with the ankle dorsiflexed (Dixon 2009 PMID 19468870. Mechanism-level reasoning from a cited mechanism, not a trial of squatting after calf strain). Plyos, jumps, sprinting, and sport change-of-direction stay frozen behind the Phase 3 hop gate. Rebuilding strength is the protection, not the risk - a residual capacity deficit is the recurrence substrate (Green 2022 PMID 35032233; Green 2017 PMID 28259848). 3) Run the two gate tests. Mon: standardized single-leg calf-raise capacity, full height, set cadence, both legs.

Done FIRST while fresh - the 7/6 30/30 is unconfirmed because the left produced less height and force. Thu: roughly 20 symptom-free single-leg hops per leg plus hop asymmetry. 5) Measure asymmetry, not just load. Every benchmark has a 10%-asymmetry half that has never been measured. Going forward: roughly 2,400-2,600 on lifting days (Mon/Wed/Fri), rest-day end on the others, protein floor 160-220 g/day (Morton 2018 PMID 28698222, Strong). 8) GET A Body-comp reading this week - 45 days blind through the program's highest-risk regain window. 9) NO DELOAD IN WEEK 21. Week 20 was involuntarily deloaded; deloading after detraining compounds the loss (Coleman 2024 PMID 38274324).

10) Label the block honestly on the site - blockLabel 'Lower rebuild', not 'Phase 3: Power Realization'. 11) Log the morning-after read. VERIFICATION NOTE for that file: Bosquet 2013 confirmed as PMID 23347054 / DOI 10.1111/sms.12047.

PMID 23529286 is a FALSE match for the McMaster strength decay-rate review - it resolves to Garth and Burke 2013 on fluid intake in competition.

Do not reuse it; the McMaster paper was not verified and is intentionally not cited. NEXT REVIEW: end of Week 21 (Sat 8/1), or immediately after the Thursday hop test if it produces gate data or a symptom. ADDENDUM (7/27, same day): the knowledge-file item above is now CLOSED - knowledge/detraining-and-return.md was written and indexed in knowledge/README.md. It carries the restart-load bands: 5-10% under the last clean set for 2-4 weeks off, 10-15% for 4-8 weeks. 15-20% for longer gaps, or an injury layoff affecting the loaded tissue. The strength-outlives-size finding justifies biasing those bands small (Psilander 2019, PMID 30991013).

scienceReviews.findings:
Wk 22 review (Tue 8/4, day 3). Window 7/27 to 8/4, eight days. And unlike the last two reviews this one is built on logged data rather than inference from a blackout: five sessions. Seven consecutive morning calf reads, and the first objective test numbers the calf block has ever produced. The gate is the only thing that closed, and the harder half did not. Monday 8/3 passed both tested criteria: 20 symptom-free single-leg hops per leg.

And 30 single-leg calf raises on each leg at 0 percent inter-limb asymmetry against a 10 percent ceiling (Green 2022 PMID 35032233. Norms referenced to Hebert-Losier 2017 PMID 28886865). Tuesday morning read calm, satisfying the 24-hour rule (Silbernagel 2007 PMID 17307888). That is two of Phase 3's four exit criteria met and the running gate open. But Green 2022's Phase 4 return-to-sport list has five items, and the loaded strength benchmarks at 10 percent asymmetry or less are untouched. Passing the endurance and hop halves is the easier half.

Finding 1, and the one with the most riding on it: the HSR line has inverted, with frequency up and intensity collapsed. Calf loading now runs 6-7x/week via the PT's daily block, which reads like excellent compliance against the 3x/week HSR target. It is not, because the block is entirely bodyweight: isometric holds, seated calf raise 3x15 unweighted, step-backs unweighted. The only genuinely loaded calf work in the last eight days is one session of single-leg calf raise. BW plus 25 lb per leg, on 7/31. Against a pre-injury baseline of seated 155 lb and single-leg BW plus 72.

And against Beyer 2015's progression from 15RM to 6RM across 12 weeks (PMID 26018970).

A bodyweight 3x15 for a 220 lb athlete is not even in 15RM territory. Morrison and Cook 2022 (PMC9124646) are explicit: if every set feels easy the load is not heavy enough. And many published protocols fail their own definition of heavy. So the HSR line is effectively running at 1x/week loaded, not 3x/week, and frequency is masking an intensity failure. Finding 2 is the same problem viewed from the gate: the soleus benchmark is unreachable on the current dose. Phase 4 wants 1.5x BW knee-flexed, roughly 330 lb at 220 lb bodyweight.

The knee-extended criterion of 1.0x BW is arguably already met at BW plus 25 single-leg. The knee-flexed one is being worked at bodyweight. This was flagged in the 7/27 review as change 6, test the soleus benchmark properly or stop claiming it. And it is still open a week later with more consequence attached. Because it is the last thing standing between two passed criteria and full clearance. It is also a PT-item conflict rather than a programming oversight, so it needs the PT's answer, not a unilateral load increase.

Finding 3: the targets are not reachable on their current horizons, and the numbers should be said out loud. Horizons run from the 3/8/2026 start, so TB DL and Squat are due 9/8/2027 and Bench 3/8/2027. TB DL needs 180 lb across 13.1 months, or 13.7 lb/month. Squat needs the same 180 lb from a current 135, so also 13.7 lb/month. Bench needs 65 lb across 7.1 months, or 9.2 lb/month. Section 7's own reality check puts months 6-12 at 2-5 lb/month on compounds, and the program is at month 5.

The observed bench rate bears that out: 155 on 5/28, 160 on 7/1, and 165 still not cleanly landed. Which is roughly 3-4 lb/month and extrapolates to about 188 by 3/2027 against a 225 target. The cause is not a training failure, it is lost calendar. Across 22 weeks the program has absorbed the Weeks 3-4 travel gap, the Weeks 19-20 travel gap. And 40 days with no barbell lower from 6/18 to 7/28, which is roughly 10 of 22 weeks. Reclaiming the pre-injury peaks is the realistic near-term goal (TB DL 245 from 6/11, Squat 160 from 6/18).

And the return-from-layoff bands make that plausible by late Aug into Sept, because strength outlives size (Psilander 2019 PMID 30991013). Past the peaks the 2-5 lb/month band bites and the target math does not close. Calf compliance: frequency target met and exceeded (3x/week required, 6-7x/week running), intensity target failed, per Finding 1. Week 21 carried three distinct calf sessions (7/28, 7/29, 7/31), the first compliant week in over a month. Volume audit for Week 21 (7/26 to 8/1) against Section 3's 6-10 hard sets per muscle. Chest 8, bench 4 at 165 plus close-grip 4, met.

Quads 6 (squat 2 hard sets at 135 on 7/28 plus 4 on 7/31) at the floor. Posterior chain 7 (TB DL 4 plus single-leg RDL 3) met. Back 5 (row only, pulldown skipped) below. Shoulders 4 and at an empty 45 lb bar, so arguably 0 hard sets, below. Core zero against a 4-6 floor, the second consecutive week at zero. The back and core misses both trace to a single cause: 7/30 was skipped entirely and took the lat pulldown and the woodchop with it.

Week 22 as now authored clears every floor at chest 8, back 8, core 6, quads 8 and posterior 7. So the fix is scheduled rather than executed. Progression: TB DL 205 clean twice (7/28, 8/3), so 215 Thursday. Which is the compound-lower double progression working normally for the first time since the restart. Squat holding 135 as a PT item. Bench holding 165 with a clean 4x5 still outstanding after two attempts (7/8 went 160/160/165/165; 7/29 went 3, 5, 3, 3).

Seated overhead press defaulted to an empty bar on 7/29 against a 95x5 standing base, corrected to 65 for Wednesday as a rebuild step. Row stepping 95 to 105, still 30 lb under the last clean pre-layoff set of 3x10x135 on 4/30. Achilles: still the non-problem. 0/10 logged on 8/3, and the tendon has not registered a symptom through the entire calf block. The green-zone streak stays paused rather than lost, pending the strain clearing. Recovery and fatigue: no reactive-deload triggers present.

RPEs are not drifting, loads are progressing, the calf gate passed, and morning reads are clean. But the fatigue read is partially blind. Because sleep has been logged twice in the last five weeks (7/28 and 7/29, both self-reported ranges recorded as 8 h estimates). So two of Section 2's seven trigger signals cannot be evaluated at all. Next scheduled deload is Week 24 (8/16 to 8/22). Coleman 2024 (PMID 38274324) says a prophylactic deload in a non-fatigued lifter costs strength, so it stays a contingency.

But non-fatigued is being asserted on incomplete data. Body comp: no reading since 6/12 (219.5 lb, 22.7 percent BF). 53 days, now the longest gap of the program, and it spans a six-week injury layoff, three weeks of travel. And 85 days of untracked intake, which is precisely the combination where recomposition reverses. The 7/27 review's change 8 asked for a reading that week; it did not happen. Nutrition: protein and calories still 0 percent logged since 5/11, now 85 days.

Separately, the anchor days are now structurally wrong. NutritionGoals set moderate-deficit days as Mon, Thu and Sat, with a rationale reading Mon equals post-Sunday-game recovery with no training. And Wed heavy TB DL plus game days Tue and Sun stay at maintenance. Every clause of that is stale: the week now runs lower on Mon, upper on Wed, lower plus the run on Thu, light on Fri. With Tue and Sat as the only non-training days and no Tue game at all. So the plan put a 2,300-2,500 cal deficit on Monday, which carries the heaviest session of the week, and held Tuesday at maintenance.

Which is a rest day. Fixed below. Worth stating plainly though: recalibrating a nutrition target that has had zero measured compliance for 85 days is bookkeeping, not intervention. The measurement is the intervention. Status of the 7/27 change list. Change 1, barbell lower restart: done and clean.

Change 2, separating barbell lower from plyo gating: done and vindicated, since 40 days off did not cost a symptom on the restart. Change 3, run the two gate tests: done, both passed. Change 4, replace 100 percent healed with the Green 2022 checklist: done and closed. And it is what made this week's decision mechanical rather than a feel call. Change 5, measure asymmetry: partial, since the capacity test logged 30 and 30 separately but hop height difference was not recorded, and the single-leg RDL. Single-leg calf raise and single-leg isometrics are still logged as one number.

Change 6, soleus benchmark: open, per Finding 2. Change 7, nutrition re-anchor: superseded by the anchor-day fix below. Change 8, body comp reading: not done, 53 days. Change 9, no Week 21 deload: done. Change 10, blockLabel Lower rebuild: done and live. Change 11, log the morning-after read: done, and it is the best data in the program.

Seven consecutive daily reads from 7/28 through 8/4 made this possible. They let the DOMS spike on 7/30 be read correctly as a 48 h peak, not an escalating trend. And what opened the gate on 8/2 and 8/3. Proof the logging habit is achievable when a single field is asked for. Test-quality caveat worth carrying: both legs stopped at exactly 30 on a test specified to fatigue. So the 0 percent asymmetry is most likely a stop-at-target artifact rather than both legs failing on the same rep.

Both criteria are met either way and 30 is a floor, but the weaker leg has still not been identified.

Run it to true failure next time. Data gaps, ranked: (1) soleus loaded-strength benchmark never tested, and now the gate's rate limiter. (2) body comp 53 days. (3) protein and calories 85 days. (4) sleep 2 nights in 5 weeks, which blinds two deload triggers. (5) single-leg loads and hop height still logged as single numbers rather than left and right.

scienceReviews.findings:
Wk 23 review (Mon 8/10, day 2), run early because the week's shape changed. Window 8/4 to 8/10. The headline, and IT IS Not about the calf: the tissue is passing everything put in front of it and the program is not running. Those are separate problems and only one of them is being worked on. Take the tissue first, because the news is good. Both gate tests passed on 8/3 on the first attempt:

20 symptom-free single-leg hops per leg. 30 single-leg calf raises on each leg at 0 percent inter-limb asymmetry against a 10 percent ceiling (Green 2022 PMID 35032233. Norms referenced to Hebert-Losier 2017 PMID 28886865). Then on 8/9 a full hockey game at high intensity with regular shifts, symptom-free start to finish. With a 1/10 calf and 1/10 Achilles read the following morning. That game is the strongest datum the whole block has produced, because hockey push-off is the strain's own injury mechanism.

Sudden knee extension with ankle dorsiflexion at push-off (Dixon 2009 PMID 19468870). The injured tissue was tested under the thing that injured it, at full intensity, and it passed. Achilles has now logged 0/10 across 30 sessions with the 8/10 morning read of 1/10 the first non-zero of the block. Which follows a high-intensity game and sits far inside the acceptable band of Silbernagel's pain-monitoring model (PMID 17307888). Day 50 post-strain. FINDING 1, The binding constraint IS Compliance, not physiology.

Lift days by week since the strain block: Wk 18 one, Wk 19 zero, Wk 20 zero, Wk 21 three, Wk 22 two. Wk 23 zero so far. That is six lift days across six weeks against roughly eighteen planned, about 33 percent. Genuinely loaded calf sessions over the same span: one, zero, zero, two, one, zero, so four against a 3x/week Beyer target that implies eighteen. The graded run has now slipped twice and the box jumps once, and both are the exposures the 8/3 gate tests specifically unlocked. So week 22 passed its criteria and then delivered nothing that depended on them.

Every previous review has diagnosed a programming problem, HSR intensity, anchor days, restart loads. And every one of those diagnoses was correct and none of them was the reason progress stalled. Volume audit against Section 3's 6-10 hard sets per muscle: Wk 22 ran chest 4, back 5, shoulders roughly 2 hard sets, quads 3. Posterior chain 11, core 0. Core has now been at zero for three consecutive weeks against a 4-6 set floor. Wk 21 was the only compliant week in two months.

FINDING 2, THE PT Relationship has ended, which closes the oldest open item and opens the calf load. The soleus-loading question has been open since 7/27 as change 6, restated 8/4 as change 2. It was blocked both times on the same thing. The daily bodyweight block was a PT prescription, and raising its load unilaterally would have overridden a clinician. That constraint is gone. The block ran 6-7x/week entirely at bodyweight, isometric holds plus seated raise 3x15 unweighted plus unweighted step-backs, against roughly 1x/week of genuinely loaded work.

For a 220 lb athlete a bodyweight 3x15 is not in 15RM territory.

Let alone the 6RM the back half of Beyer 2015's protocol calls for (PMID 26018970). And Morrison and Cook 2022 (PMC9124646) are explicit that if every set feels easy the load is not heavy enough. Frequency was being counted as compliance while intensity failed. That is now fixable and is fixed below. FINDING 3, The soleus benchmark needs AN Explicit judgment call rather than another deferral. Green 2022's Phase 4 return-to-sport list has five criteria.

Four are met or close: VAS is 0/10 through the block, calf-raise capacity is 30 reps at 0 percent asymmetry. Hop asymmetry passed on symptoms and rep count though height difference was never measured. And the knee-extended strength criterion of 1.0x BW is met at single-leg BW plus 25, which is roughly 245 against a 220 lb bodyweight. The fifth is the knee-flexed soleus benchmark at 1.5x BW, roughly 330 lb of external load on a seated raise. Current is 135 and the pre-injury baseline was 155, which is about 0.7x BW. At two loaded sessions a week with a load step every second clean session.

Closing that gap is realistically six to nine months of consistent work. It is reachable, but not before any near-term basketball decision, so continuing to treat it as a hard gate means never returning. Calling that out explicitly rather than letting it sit open for a fourth review. FINDING 4, Target arithmetic, now resolved. Horizons run from the 3/8/2026 start. On the old horizons bench needed 8.7 lb/month to reach 225x5 by 3/2027, TB DL needed 14 lb/month to reach 385x5 by 9/2027.

And squat needed 14 lb/month to reach 315x5 on the same date. Section 7's reality check puts months 6-12 at 2-5 lb/month on compounds and the program is at month 5. Observed bench rate is 4-5 lb/month, which is squarely inside that band, so the rate is not the problem. About 10 of the program's first 23 weeks were absorbed by two travel gaps. A six-week calf layoff that took 40 days of barbell lower with it. The shortfall is lost calendar.

Resolved below by moving the calendar rather than the numbers. FINDING 5, Data capture has been asked for and not delivered, SO The asks are being cut rather than repeated. Nutrition: 91 days with no protein or calorie entry, since 5/11, across two separate revisions of the anchor days. Sleep: two nights logged in five weeks, which blinds two of the seven reactive-deload triggers. Body composition: last reading 6/12 at 219.5 lb and 22.7 percent, now 59 days, the longest gap of the program, spanning an injury layoff. Travel and three months of untracked intake, which is exactly the combination where recomposition reverses.

Three consecutive reviews have asked for a body-comp reading. The pattern is clear enough to act on.
