scienceReviews.findings:
WEEK 24 REVIEW, run 8/18 at the athlete's request before any frequency change. This also covers Week 23, whose Saturday review never ran.

COMPLIANCE, AND A CORRECTION TO THE PREMISE OF The two-day rule. Delivered lift sessions by week: wk18 1, wk19 0 (travel), wk20 0 (travel), wk21 3, wk22 3, wk23 2. Weeks 21, 22 and 23 each met or exceeded plan, which is three consecutive complete weeks. The Wk 23 review on 8/10 recorded the sequence as '1, 0, 0, 3, 2 and 0' and concluded the program averaged one lift day. And that finding is what set the two-gym-day rule. That count was taken mid-week-23, before 8/13 and 8/14 ran, and it read wk22 as 2 rather than 3.

The corrected picture is that the compliance collapse was weeks 18 to 20, which were one bad week plus two travel weeks. Not a standing pattern. Compliance is no longer the binding constraint. This is the single most important input to the frequency question and it changes the answer.

HSR FREQUENCY IS The real gap. Genuinely loaded calf sessions by week: wk18 2, wk21 2, wk22 1, wk23 2. Against Beyer's 3x/week (PMID 26018970) the program has never once hit three. Every week since the restart has been short, and wk22 delivered one. The 8/14 single-leg raise was the first session ever confirmed as a true rep max.

VOLUME BY PATTERN, wk23: squat 4, hinge 7, horizontal push 6, vertical push 3, horizontal pull 3, vertical pull 2, core 6. Vertical push, horizontal pull and vertical pull all sit below Section 3's 6-10 floor. That was the stated and accepted cost of two gym days.

PROGRESSION. Bench press is working: 155 to 170 since 6/10, which is +8.3 lb/month and above Section 7's 2-5 lb/month band for months 6-12. Trap bar deadlift is 215, still 30 lb under the 245 pre-injury peak. Back squat is the problem: 135 on 7/28, 7/31 and 8/13, so ZERO PROGRESSION IN 4.2 MONTHS, and 25 lb under the 160 pre-injury peak. Squat has run once a week since the restart. And Schoenfeld 2016 (PMID 27102172) found two sessions per week per muscle beat one at matched volume.

The most likely cause of the squat stall is frequency, not load selection.

PAIN. AM reads 8/10 and 8/11 at 1/10 on the left Achilles, then 0/10 on 8/12, 8/13 and 8/14. In-session Achilles 0/10 across eight consecutive entries, including both games on 8/16. No week-to-week climb, so the Silbernagel pain rule (PMID 17307888) stays satisfied. The 8/14 lower back episode cleared over the weekend and held through both games. Which identifies it as a positional failure inside one set rather than a tissue problem.

RETURN TO SPORT. Basketball returned 8/16 after 56 days, at 20 minutes and half intensity, symptom-free, followed by 60 minutes of hockey at high intensity, also symptom-free. Against Green 2022's Phase 4 list (PMID 35032233), four of five criteria are met: VAS 0/10. Calf raise 30 reps at 0 percent asymmetry on 8/3, hop asymmetry inside 10 percent, and a completed symptom-free sport exposure. Which the two 8/16 games supply even though the 8/13 box jumps read 1-3/10. The outstanding criterion IS The knee-flexed soleus benchmark of 1.5x body weight, roughly 330 lb.

The seated calf raise is at 150, moving to 165. That is the one genuine intensity gap in the program and it is not close.

BODY COMPOSITION. Last reading 6/12 at 219.5 lb and 22.7 percent, now 67 days ago. Trend from 4/22 to 6/12 was 221.6 to 219.5 lb and 23.3 to 22.7 percent, so slow movement in the intended direction. There is no data since, across an injury layoff, travel and a return to sport. Asked for in four consecutive reviews.

The frequency versus intensity question, answered from the evidence. Frequency is the supported lever and intensity is not. Pelland 2026 (PMID 41343037) found volume's diminishing returns considerably more pronounced for strength than for size, while frequency showed a consistent positive effect on strength. Robinson 2024 (PMID 38970765) found strength gains similar across a wide range of repetitions in reserve. So pushing sets closer to failure does not buy strength. Load intensity is already adequate: the working loads sit above the 75 percent of 1RM threshold Suchomel 2018 (PMID 29372481) requires to hold strength-power qualities.

Adding a third day and holding the per-pattern set counts raises frequency without a volume spike, which is what Gabbett 2016 (PMID 26758673) cautions against. Note the transfer caveat: Pelland's sample averaged 25.2 years old.

The soleus criterion is still the laggard. Green 2022 (PMID 35032233) sets knee-flexed strength at 1.5x body weight or more. At 222.9 lb that is about 334 lb. The seated calf raise sits at 165 lb, which is 0.74x body weight. It has moved 150 to 165 and now steps to 180.

The gap is still large. Whether the machine's load range even reaches 334 lb is unverified. That limit needs checking rather than assuming.

New symptom, right calf. Tight on the morning of 8/24, after Sunday's 20 minutes of high-intensity basketball. Pain 1 to 2 out of 10, worst on the eccentric lowering from a toe stand. No swelling. No difference in size or shape versus the left.

This is the leg that took the minor pull on 6/21 and was played through. It is not the leg that tore.

No red flags are present. Pain is not out of proportion to the exam. There is no tense compartment, so compartment syndrome is not indicated (Pechar and Lyons 2016). There is no swelling or inter-limb asymmetry, which lowers DVT probability (Wells 1997, PMID 9428249). The presentation is consistent with post-game soreness or low-grade reactive tightness.

It stays monitored. Green 2017 (PMID 28259848, Strong) identifies increasing age and previous calf injury as the two strongest recurrence risks. This leg carries a prior event, and the athlete is 40.

Asymmetry is reported but never measured under load. On 8/21 the athlete reported the left leg, the strained side, felt weaker than the right. Green 2022 gates return on 10% or less inter-limb asymmetry. The 7/6 capacity test showed 30 reps on each leg, so the rep-count gate passed. A bodyweight rep test is insensitive to a loaded strength deficit, so that result does not close the question.

Squat stall is broken. The lift held 135 lb for 4.2 months. It ran 135 on 7/31, 8/13 and 8/18, then a clean 3x5 at 145 on 8/20. The 2x per week change is the plausible cause (Schoenfeld 2016, PMID 27102172, two sessions beat one at matched volume). Only one clean session sits at 145, so double progression holds it one more week.

Calibration sets are earning their place. The trap bar gave 10 reps at 215, hitting the hard cap, so the load steps 20 lb to 235. The bench gave 7 reps at 175, so it steps 5 lb to 180. Both loads had drifted light, which is the drift Halperin 2022 (PMID 34542869) predicts from RIR estimation.

Week 24 ran two reps-plus sets, on separate days, with the lower-body set on the earlier day. That matches the placement rule.

A compliance failure mode is now visible. Friday 8/21 carried nine exercises and the two core items were dropped. The 8/18 review had cut Friday to six items. The physique goal then added three isolation lifts and put it back to nine. Given the choice, the athlete kept the new isolation work and cut the core work.

Overhead press stepped too fast. The prescription was 3x6 at the 40s, off a clean 3x6 at the 35s. It delivered 5 and 5 at 40, then a drop to 35 for 5. The load moved before the reps were owned.

Body composition has one data point. The 8/18 reading was 222.9 lb at 23.5%. The first scheduled Saturday weigh-in, on 8/22, did not happen. The stated rule needs three consecutive same-direction readings, or a change above 4 lb, before a trend is callable. Nothing is callable yet.

That is expected this early in a weekly series.

Achilles is quiet. Every logged session in week 24 read 0 out of 10, and both games read 0. No regression signal against the Silbernagel monitoring model. Morning reads in bodyLog stopped after 8/14, though session-level pain is still captured.

Nutrition was not reviewed, per the standing rule.

WHAT IT IS AND IS NOT: both signals are individually sub-threshold. 1/10 sits deep inside the 0-3/10 acceptable band where the decision tree says continue the protocol. And 15-30 min of stiffness is above the program's typical under-15 min but below the over-30 min regression threshold. Two mild sub-threshold signals point the same direction on the same side. Not worth acting on yet. Most likely driver: Sunday's hockey. It is the only meaningful load in the window, it was the first full high-intensity game of the block. And hockey is push-off and plantarflexion heavy, so a tendon response 24-48 h out is mechanistically expected. Nothing else has loaded the tendon since 8/6. What does not follow: backing off the loaded calf work. HSR is the treatment for Achilles tendinopathy rather than something to withdraw at 1/10. Beyer 2015's protocol runs through mild pain by design (PMID 26018970). And pulling load at the first 1/10 is the exact instinct that kept this block under-loaded for six weeks. Today's loaded single-leg session goes, holding BW plus 25 rather than progressing. The read to watch is tomorrow's: escalation past 3/10, or stiffness crossing 30 min, changes the answer.

Morning read: back to 0/10, left Achilles clear, no stiffness reported. This closes the two-day tendon signal. The 8/10 and 8/11 reads were both 1/10 on the left Achilles with 15-30 min of stiffness on the second. Against a block baseline of 0/10 across 30 logged sessions. The concern on 8/11 was specifically that it had not cleared at roughly 48 h. Silbernagel's 24-hour rule expects a return to pre-exercise baseline (PMID 17307888). It cleared at roughly 72 h post-game. Read as a delayed but complete settle after the first full high-intensity hockey game of the block. Not a step change in the tendon. And the decision made on 8/11, hold the loaded calf work at BW+25 rather than withdraw it. Was the right call by outcome. One caveat on what this read is worth: Tuesday's prescribed loaded single-leg session did not happen. Monday's run did not happen either. This follows two days with no calf loading at all. Read it as a floor, not a tolerance test. The same caveat that applied to 8/5.

Morning read: 0/10, second consecutive clean read. This is the read the box jumps were gated on, and at 0/10 it cleared the under-3/10 criterion outright. So the plyometric exposure ran. Also follows a second day with no calf loading, since Wednesday's run was skipped. So like 8/12 it is a floor read. Today's session is the tolerance test.

Morning read: 0/10, third consecutive clean read. This is roughly 24 h after the largest combined lower-body exposure since the 6/21 strain. 4x3 step-down box jumps off an 18 in box. Trap bar deadlift 4x5 at 215, back squat 4x5 at 135 and seated calf raise 3x10 at 150. THIS IS The read that settles thursday. The left medial gastroc registered 1-3/10 during the jumps themselves. Silbernagel's model accepts up to 5/10 during loading. It must return to baseline inside 24 h and not climb week to week (PMID 17307888). It returned to baseline. So the jumps cost nothing measurable and the 150 lb seated calf step is validated at the tissue level. What the clean read does NOT do is retroactively make the exposure symptom-free. Which is the wording Green 2022's Phase 4 checklist uses (PMID 35032233). Clean reads now run 7/31, 8/2, 8/3, 8/4, 8/5, 8/12, 8/13 and 8/14. With the only non-zero readings of the block being 8/10 and 8/11 at 1/10, both resolved. No week-to-week climb.

The lower back cleared, and then held under sport. Friday's row produced sharp pain at rep 10 of a set prescribed at 5, still present 30 minutes later. By the weekend there was nothing. It then held through 20 minutes of basketball and 60 minutes of hockey with no symptoms. That reads as a positional failure inside one set rather than a tissue problem. So the answer is to cap the row at 5 reps rather than to withdraw loaded hinging. The calf and achilles answered A Bigger question today. Basketball returned after 56 days. And the athlete self-limited to 20 minutes at roughly half intensity rather than waiting for a strictly symptom-free box jump. Friday's jumps had read 1-3/10 in the left gastroc, which left Green 2022's Phase 4 wording unsatisfied (PMID 35032233). So the strict checklist never cleared. A graded, self-limited re-entry is arguably the better instrument: it produces a tolerance datum at a controlled dose. Where a binary gate produces only a pass or a fail. Both games were symptom-free, and the hockey game was the larger demand at 60 minutes and high intensity. No morning read was reported for 8/15 or 8/16. Saturday delivered nothing: no calf block, no Week 23 science review, and no body-composition reading. Which is now 65 days out.

First body-composition reading IN 67 DAYS, AND IT IS A REVERSAL. 222.9 lb at 23.5 percent, against 219.5 lb at 22.7 percent on 6/12. Weight is up 3.4 lb, or 1.5 percent of body weight, and body fat is up 0.8 points. Decomposed: FAT MASS 49.8 to 52.4 lb, so plus 2.6 lb. LEAN MASS 169.7 to 170.5 lb, so plus 0.8 lb. THIS IS NOT NOISE. The rule in knowledge/body-composition-measurement.md: act only on a sustained move above 1 percent of body weight. It has to hold across two or more weeks. And this is 1.5 percent across 67 days. Weight and body-fat percentage also moved in the same direction. A hydration or glycogen artifact would not do that as cleanly. Bhutani 2017 (PMID 28701524) puts roughly 84 percent of short-term weight change in fat-free mass. That is why single-direction agreement across both measures matters. Consumer BIA misestimates absolute fat mass against DEXA, so the deltas carry the signal and the absolute numbers do not. The arc across the program. First reading 3/11 was 218.3 lb at 22.7 percent. April to mid-June trended slowly the right way, 221.6 to 219.5 lb and 23.3 to 22.7 percent. The 67 days since erased that and more. Current standing is 4.6 lb heavier and 0.8 points fatter than the first reading of the program, 160 days in. THE CAUSE IS The window, not the training. Those 67 days contain a 40-day gap without barbell lower, weeks 19 and 20 with zero logged training. And no intake data at all since 5/11. Training volume collapsed. Intake almost certainly did not. The one good signal IS LEAN MASS. It rose 0.8 lb across an injury layoff, which is what the strength work was there to protect. And it did. GAP TO Target has widened. Against 210 lb and 15 percent, that is now 12.9 lb and 8.5 points. Which is roughly 22 lb of fat at constant lean mass. That is a six to nine month job at a sustainable rate, and it cannot be driven by training.

Second reading of the weekly series, 6 days after 8/18. Weight is up 3.1 lb and body fat is up 0.7 points. Off the usual Saturday slot, since the 8/22 weigh-in did not happen, so conditions may not match exactly. The stated rule needs three consecutive same-direction readings, or a change above 4 lb, before a trend is callable. This single reading does not clear either bar. Two readings and 6 days is not enough to call anything yet.

21.title: Barbell lower restart, criteria-gated
21.subtitle: Barbell lower restarted Tuesday at the reduced load and went clean. Both gate tests postponed again, to Monday 8/3, after Thursday's read climbed to 3-5/10.
21.reason:
Week 21 carries the first barbell lower session since 6/18, after 39 days off. Day 36 post-strain.

Three facts reshape the block. Basketball is in its off-season, so the Tuesday game is gone. Sunday AM basketball stays held until the calf clears. Weeks 19 and 20 were travel with little training logged. Only hockey on Sunday 8/2 remains, so the in-season volume ceiling largely lifts.

Restart loads are cut roughly 15 percent: trap bar deadlift 245 to 205, and squat 160 to 135. Two clean sessions earn plus 10 on the lower compounds.

Barbell lower is not the calf risk here. Jumps, sprinting and change of direction are. The trap bar deadlift is hip-dominant, and the squat bottom flexes the knee, which slackens the gastroc. So barbell lower returns now, while jumps stay frozen behind the hop gate.

Two gate tests this week, because "until the calf is 100 percent" has no exit criterion. Monday: single-leg calf-raise capacity, both legs. Thursday: roughly 20 symptom-free hops per leg, plus asymmetry.

Pain rule: up to 5/10 during loading and the next morning, settling within 24 hours, and not climbing week to week. No static end-range calf stretching.

schedule.longDesc: No game. Basketball is in its off-season, and Sunday AM play stays self-gated until the calf clears the hop criteria.

schedule.desc: Rest, lower restart moved to Tue
schedule.longDesc: Rest day taken. The prescribed lower restart moved to Tuesday PM and the capacity test did not run at all. Left on the board as the record of what was prescribed. Original plan: run the capacity test first, while fresh, because a to-fatigue test after deadlifts measures fatigue rather than capacity. Then trap bar deadlift at the reduced restart load, then the calf work.

exercises.name: Single-leg calf-raise to fatigue (capacity test)
exercises.notes: Do this first, fresh. Standardize what 7/6 did not: full height every rep, roughly 2 seconds per rep, knee straight. Stop when height drops or form breaks. Record reps left and right. The gate is 30 or more reps at 10 percent or less asymmetry. Treat the 7/6 result of 30/30 as unconfirmed. Floor range, no heel drop below neutral.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.notes: Restart load, ~15% under the 6/11 4x5x245, after 39 days off. RPE 6-7, leave 3-4 reps in reserve. Two clean sessions earn +10. Do not chase 245 this week. ROM: full range from the floor, heels flat, hips loaded.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (HSR)
exercises.notes: Anchored to the 7/8 load because nothing is logged in the 19 days since. If you worked above 135 during the gap, log the real number and we re-anchor. Step to 145 only after a clean morning-after read. ROM: knee bent, full plantarflexion, controlled pain-free bottom, no forced stretch.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise (HSR)
exercises.notes: Matches 7/8. Pre-injury was bodyweight plus 72. At roughly 1.11x bodyweight this nominally clears the knee-extended strength benchmark, but the asymmetry half is unmeasured. Compare left and right honestly and log them separately. Floor range only, no heel drop below neutral until stair descent is pain-free.

exercises.notes: Proximal chain, calf-sparing. ROM: full, controlled, no snapping at end range.

In the afternoon both barbell lower lifts came back in one session, the first since 6/18. Trap bar deadlift 4x5x205 landed clean, one session toward the step to 215. Back squat was pulled forward from Friday, ramped 45/95/135 and held 135 for two sets. It is not yet a clean 4x5.

Calf work diverged from the plan, under clinical direction. The PT gave a home program at the morning visit, and the isometric standing holds came from it. Seated raises ran two reps heavier per set. The loaded single-leg calf raise was skipped, so the knee-extended benchmark and the countable asymmetry number are both still missing. The capacity test did not run either.

Calf silent through the session. Wednesday's read was 1-2/10 diffuse, inside the pain rule.

exercises.notes: PT-prescribed. 4.5 minutes of total hold time across both blocks. Single-leg holds do expose left against right qualitatively. A hold gives no rep count and no force number. It satisfies neither the strength benchmark nor the asymmetry criterion.

16.title: INJURED - acute calf strain (Phase 0 protection)
16.subtitle: Left calf strain on June 21. Phase 3 is paused. This week is protected weight-bearing plus an in-person exam. No games, no calf loading.
16.reason:
Sunday's basketball produced a minor right-calf pull that was played through, then minutes later an acute, severe left-calf strain, the classic 'tennis leg' pattern. Difficulty bearing weight since means at least a Grade II strain.

The first priority is an in-person exam before any programming. That exam needs to rule out an Achilles rupture with the calf-squeeze test. A rupture can still let someone walk and weakly push off, which makes it easy to miss. The exam also needs to rule out a blood clot, which shows up in about 1 in 10 similar injuries. Seek emergency care if the pain is out of proportion to the exam, with a tense, swollen calf.

Acute care follows protect-elevate-compress-educate, then load-optimism-vascularization-exercise. A short course of ibuprofen is fine for pain, then switch to acetaminophen as pain eases; don't run an anti-inflammatory for weeks. Early, gentle loading beats full immobilization, so pain-free range-of-motion work starts now, with pain-free isometrics late this week.

HSR drops to zero and rebuilds later, not at the pre-injury loads. Recurrence risk is high at this age with a prior calf injury on record. Every step of this rehab is gated on meeting a criterion, not a calendar date.

17.title: Calf rehab Phase 1 + calf-sparing leg/upper strength
17.subtitle: Calf rehab holds at the current load, since mornings still linger. Legs stay working with calf-sparing lifts, plus an upper day. No calf-loading compounds, no games.
17.reason:
Phase 1 begins once the athlete walks without a limp, isometrics are pain-free, and the serious differentials are excluded. Progress moves from isometrics to double-leg to single-leg calf raises through a tolerable range. HSR reintroduces at a markedly reduced load, rebuilt rather than resumed at the pre-injury level. Pain rule: stay at or below 5 out of 10 during and the next morning, with no week-to-week increase. No games this week; calf strains can recur without warning.

Update: the calf is improving but sitting at a load ceiling. Morning-after pain still lingers past 24 hours, and stair descent still produces an occasional sharp twinge. This week holds the rehab load; any increase waits on a clean morning first.

Upper body and calf-sparing lower work can still train: leg extension, hip thrust, and back extension. Every calf-loading compound stays on hold until Phase 2: squat, deadlift, leg press, lunges, split squats, heavy leg curls, and all jumping or running. A deep squat and a heavy deadlift both cross the knee and ankle, asking more than this strain can take yet.

Recurrence risk is highest at this age with a calf injury on record, so nothing here loads on feel alone.

18.title: Calf: Phase 2 strength and monitored return to games
18.subtitle: Confirm-and-protect: measure single-leg capacity, keep loading the calf, watch the morning-after read after games. Barbell lower stays frozen until the capacity gate clears.
18.reason:
This week shifts from straight rehab to confirm-and-protect. Sunday's off-plan hockey game was tolerated well: light morning soreness that settled within 24 hours, better than the prior pattern. That clears the gate the last review was waiting on, so cautious continued play is fine, and games are back to top priority.

But that return got ahead of the actual return-to-sport tests, still unmeasured. The tests are 30 or more single-leg calf-raise reps, 10% or less side-to-side difference, and calf strength benchmarks. A deficit can persist after pain is gone, and that gap drives recurrence. Recurrence strikes without warning and is more likely at this age with a prior calf injury.

This week does three things. First, measure single-leg capacity while fresh, the one hard number still missing. Second, keep loading the calf toward the pre-injury level, since loading the deficit out protects against recurrence more than rest does. Third, log pain during and after every game; light and settling means keep going, lingering or climbing means pull back to rehab.

De-risk every game with a full calf warm-up and an eased-in push-off, and stop on any sharp pain. Barbell lower lifts stay frozen until the capacity gate clears.
